ai.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
ai.brief: The Anthropic IPO raises big questions about the future of AI, the company’s safety-first mission, and how we balance idealism with capitalism. Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders.

sec.title: Cairn AI Framework Used in Autonomous Zero-Day Exploitation
sec.brief: S. S. CISA adds Apache Axis, Vanderbilt REDCap,BerriAI LiteLLM, and Synology DSM flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Norwegian Gas Giant Equinor Says It's Under Cyberattack. S. CISA adds Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Amazon’s threat intelligence team found a Chinese-nexus actor running Cairn, an open-source AI pentesting framework, with one instruction for the agents: obtain shell access. No human chose the next step after that. The agents planned, executed, and adjusted on their own, and along the way they found a real zero-day in an open-source medical imaging application.
